Package model.filesystem

Class FileSystem

java.lang.Object
model.filesystem.FileSystem
public class FileSystem extends Object
Represents a complete Unix-style in-memory file system implementation.

This class is the main coordinator for the richer file system model. It manages path validation, inode resolution, directory hierarchy operations, file creation and updates, permission changes, search utilities, logging, and storage accounting through the SuperBlock.

The design follows familiar Unix concepts: a root directory, absolute paths, inode metadata, owner/group permissions, recursive directory traversal, and command-like operations such as mkdir, cp, mv, chmod, and rm. Data is kept in memory for educational purposes, while operational events are written to the file system logger.

  • Method Details

    • createFile

      public void createFile(String path, String content, String owner) throws FileSystemException
      Creates a file at the specified path with content.

      The method validates the absolute path, resolves the parent directory, prevents duplicate file names, allocates block and inode resources, and finally attaches the new file inode to its parent directory.

      Parameters:
      path - the absolute file path, for example /home/user/file.txt
      content - the file content; null is converted to an empty string
      owner - the logical owner assigned to the file
      Throws:
      FileSystemException - if the path is invalid, the parent directory does not exist, the entry already exists, or there is not enough simulated space

    • deleteEntry

      public void deleteEntry(String path) throws FileSystemException
      Deletes a file or empty directory.

      Root deletion is rejected. Directory deletion is allowed only when the directory has no children; callers that need recursive deletion should use deleteRecursive(String) instead.

      Parameters:
      path - the absolute path to delete
      Throws:
      FileSystemException - if the path is invalid, the target does not exist, the target is root, or the directory is not empty

    • changePermissions

      public void changePermissions(String path, String permissions) throws FileSystemException
      Changes file permissions.

      Permissions are expressed with the traditional three-digit octal style: owner, group, and others. For example, 755 grants full owner permissions and read/execute permissions to group and others.

      Parameters:
      path - the absolute file or directory path
      permissions - the permissions in three-digit octal form, for example 755 or 644
      Throws:
      FileSystemException - if the path is invalid, permissions are malformed, or the entry does not exist

    • resolveInode

      public Inode resolveInode(String path)
      Resolves a path to its inode.

      Resolution starts at the root inode and walks each path segment in order. Invalid paths or missing segments return null instead of throwing, which makes this method convenient for existence checks.

      Parameters:
      path - the absolute file or directory path
      Returns:
      the matching inode, or null if not found
